title: Single-cell 3D genome imaging shows super-enhancer hubs are rare; nonspecific; and neither necessary nor sufficient for transcriptional bursting.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 10472228 (CC-BY-4.0, single version v0.0.0 dated 2024-04-25, titled after the bioRxiv preprint). Listed all 6 files and their sizes; read the zip directories by ranged GET (80 per-FOV, i.e. per field-of-view, CSVs at ~10 MB each; the FOF-CT tables: all_E14mESC core 331 MB and quality 220 MB uncompressed). Pulled out and parsed the three RNA_DNA tables: 138,795 spot rows, 45 FOVs, ~1,737 cells (FOV x Cell_ID), 42 loci. Nascent-RNA burst intensity is present for only 15,411 allele rows across 6 genes; 2,650 of them are >0. Opened SuperEnhancerLoci.xlsx (376 super-enhancers, mm10 and mm9 coordinates, gene names, RefSeq IDs) and the chromatin-feature xlsx (376 rows: NANOG/OCT4/SOX2/Pol II/MED1 ChIP, H3K27ac, LAD and SPRITE-speckle scores).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available (paywalled, not in PMC). The cohesin, CTCF, BET and Pol II perturbation datasets and the 'thousands of cells' figure come from the abstract; the perturbation data is not in the Zenodo deposit I opened, which predates the final paper. The large all_E14mESC tables were not downloaded (over 50 MB).

a1_downloadable.note: Open Zenodo record under CC-BY-4.0, no login; checked in the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The bursting label is a measured column (nascentRNA_burst_intensity, one per allele). Hub membership, by contrast, would have to be built from 3D distances, so only bursting counts as a ready-made label.

a3_inputs_present.note: The inputs are x/y/z coordinates in microns for each imaged locus, plus 1D chromatin scores for all 376 super-enhancers. No identifier lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: The header says XYZ_unit=micron and genome build mm10. Burst intensity is in arbitrary fluorescence units (0 to 59,059), so a yes/no burst threshold is safer.

a5_enough_rows.note: 15,411 allele observations with a burst measurement (2,650 bursting) pass the 400-row classification bar. But they cover only 6 genes in ~1,737 cells, so the effective diversity is tiny.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~35 MB uncompressed for the RNA+DNA tables; ~550 MB if you add the full DNA-only tracing tables
a6_fits_laptop.note: Plain CSVs; the RNA_DNA subset loads in seconds.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 376 super-enhancers and >1,700 cells fit 'hundreds of SEs in thousands of cells'. The perturbation data mentioned in the abstract is missing from this 2024 deposit, which is a version gap, not a contradiction.

a8_label_provenance.note: Burst intensity is a direct physical measurement (nascent-RNA FISH signal at each allele). It is not a model output and is not computed from the DNA coordinates.

B1.why: Three FOF-CT tables (core, quality, cell) joined on Spot_ID; hub features must be computed from coordinates. Seen in files.

B2.why: CSVs with '#' comment headers and a parenthesised column line; needs skiprows and manual column names. Seen.

B3.why: One lab and one assay, but burst intensity is in arbitrary units; a threshold or per-gene normalisation is needed.

B4.why: No censored values; 85% of zeros are real 'no burst' calls. Seen in files.

B5.why: Spot_IDs are unique; no duplicates seen in the RNA_DNA tables.

B6.why: FOF-CT format is documented online and the header names the columns, but the burst calling threshold is undocumented.

C1.why: Asking whether 3D neighbourhood predicts bursting beyond hub presence is informative, but the paper already reports a weak effect.

C2.why: Rajpurkar 2021 deep-learning trace-to-transcription model exists, open code, Drosophila data only; nothing on mouse SEs found.

C3.why: Weak unique-application/transfer angle: test fly-trained trace-to-transcription approach on mouse super-enhancers.

C4.why: ORCA (multiplexed DNA plus RNA imaging) needs weeks of microscopy per experiment.

C5.why: Obvious dummies: per-gene burst rate, and linear distance to the nearest SE; no published AUC from this paper seen.

D1.why: No open pretrained backbone for single-cell 3D coordinate traces; DNA models don't fit 6 genes.

D2.why: Nothing to freeze; a model would be trained from scratch (graph network or gradient boosting on distances).

D3.why: Data is CC-BY-4.0 per the Zenodo record.

E1.why: Hold out by field of view (45 FOVs) or by gene; both split cleanly.

E2.why: Only 6 genes with burst labels; holding out genes leaves too few groups.

E3.why: Per-gene burst-rate baseline is trivial to compute.

E4.why: No replicate measurements per allele; noise floor not estimable from these files.

E5.why: Known effect: two alleles in one cell co-burst more, and the paper reports larger hubs slightly raise burst probability.

E6.why: Label shuffling within gene, and dropping the coordinate features, are both straightforward.

E7.why: No second mouse SE RNA+DNA imaging set found; Drosophila ORCA data is a different system.

E8.why: Full text unavailable; can't confirm which published numbers to reproduce.

G1.why: mm10 genomic coordinates and RefSeq IDs for all 376 super-enhancers, seen in xlsx.

G2.why: 4DN portal chromatin-tracing data and ENCODE mESC tracks are plausible partners; not verified joinable for bursting.

G3.why: Coordinate overlap of 15 kb SE regions is one-to-one with genomic bins.

G4.why: No combination answers a bigger question that neither answers alone; the chromatin features are already included.

H1.why: Negatives present: 12,761 non-bursting allele observations versus 2,650 bursting. Seen.

H2.why: One lab, one cell line (E14 mouse ES cells), 6 genes.

H4.why: Gene count for RNA readout only visible in files; abstract implies broader coverage.

I1.why: 3D-genome and enhancer-biology community (e.g. 4DN consortium); no decision hinges on it.

I2.why: The paper already settles the biological question; a model would not redirect experiments.

I3.why: Burst yes/no AUC roughly matches 'does structure predict activity'.

I4.why: Paper finds weak signal; per-gene rate plus distance threshold likely matches any model.

J1.why: Geometric feature engineering and grouped CV, but no transfer learning.

J2.why: Boettiger lab is at Stanford, same institution as user; domain is specialist.

J3.why: Negative result 'structure adds nothing beyond gene identity' is shareable but thin.

J4.why: One-week scope is plausible but not stated.

existing_models.name: Rajpurkar et al. 2021, deep learning connecting DNA traces to transcription (Nature Communications)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicted on/off expression state from Drosophila ORCA traces of the Bithorax complex and beat contact-based methods; exact AUC and split not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Retrieved summary says single enhancer-promoter contacts contribute little and predictive features go beyond contact; full discussion not read.

backbone.name: none suitable
backbone.hardware: CPU; gradient boosting or a small graph network on pairwise distances

integration.partner_dataset: 4DN Data Portal chromatin-tracing (FOF-CT) datasets; ENCODE mESC ChIP-seq (already summarised in the deposit)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None convincing: the 1D chromatin features worth joining are already in the deposit, and no other mouse SE RNA+DNA imaging set was found.

controls.positive_control: Recover the per-gene burst rate, and the allele co-bursting and hub-size effects the paper reports.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle burst labels within gene; replace coordinates with noise of the same shape.
controls.external_validation: None for mouse; Drosophila ORCA RNA+DNA data (Mateo 2019) only as a cross-system transfer test.

honest_claim_h3: Within E14 mouse ES cells and 6 imaged genes, the model measures how much the 3D positions of 376 super-enhancers around an allele add to predicting a nascent-RNA burst beyond gene identity.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the imaged 3D positions of hundreds of strong enhancers around a gene copy to predict whether that copy is actively transcribing.
plain_idea.train_on: For each gene copy in a single cell, the distances to the 376 imaged super-enhancers plus their chromatin scores; 15,411 labelled copies across 6 genes and ~1,737 cells (verified).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the copy shows a nascent-RNA burst, measured by RNA FISH (fluorescent probes against newly made RNA) imaged in the same cell.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would test whether any 3D spatial pattern, not just hub presence, carries information about bursting. The paper already suggests the answer is 'barely', so the expected payoff is small.

more_or_better_data.why: Mouse super-enhancers across 376 loci versus Rajpurkar's single Drosophila locus, but the RNA label covers only 6 genes here.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurements per allele, and only 6 genes, so calibrated per-group uncertainty is not supportable.

models_beatable.why: The 2021 model was trained on a different organism and locus. It's not a direct competitor, and its split wasn't retrieved.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model is trained on this task and data, and there's no joinable new data measuring the same quantity the same way.

label_elsewhere.sources: 4DN Data Portal holds other chromatin-tracing sets, some with RNA readouts (known resource, not searched for mESC bursting); Drosophila ORCA RNA+DNA (Mateo 2019, known).
label_elsewhere.why: Burst labels from other imaging studies are at other loci and in other species, so they serve only for cross-system transfer tests, not as extra training data.

ambitious.why: It would need to show that 3D super-enhancer configuration predicts bursting well beyond gene identity, which contradicts the paper; unlikely.

realistic.why: Publishes reanalysis notes such as a grouped-CV benchmark of structure-to-transcription prediction on public 4DN tracing data.

fallback.why: A negative result, 'structure adds little beyond gene identity', fits a short preprint.

pitch.headline: Rare paired data: 3D positions of 376 super-enhancers plus same-cell nascent-RNA bursts in ~1,737 mouse ES cells, CC-BY, 35 MB.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: The same cells have both their DNA positions and their burst calls (15,411 allele observations), in a documented 4DN format, freely licensed. Most public tracing sets lack the RNA readout.
pitch.the_win: A grouped-by-FOV model whose burst AUC beats the per-gene-rate baseline by a clear margin, which would show that 3D context carries signal the paper's hub analysis missed.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A clean quantitative confirmation that super-enhancer 3D configuration adds little beyond gene identity. Modest: the paper already says this.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Boettiger lab (Stanford) and 4DN chromatin-tracing groups debating the condensate/hub model. It would sharpen, not change, their conclusions.

ml_idea: Per-allele burst classification from distances to 376 SEs plus 1D chromatin scores, with grouped CV by FOV. Compare against per-gene burst rate and nearest-SE distance baselines; optionally test transfer to Drosophila ORCA.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from parsed table sizes (138,795 spot rows); no model was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Fit per-gene burst rate alone and add distance-to-nearest-SE. If AUC rises by under 0.02 on FOV-grouped CV, stop.

verdict_reason: Part A passes, but bursting is measured for only 6 genes, no pretrained backbone fits (D fails), and the paper already reports the 3D-to-bursting signal is weak. Low payoff unless the perturbation data appears on 4DN.
